A Cameroonian novelist and essayist whose satires of colonial rule and missionaries, such as The Poor Christ of Bomba (1956), made him a major voice of African literature in French.

He lived in France for decades as a teacher. His essay Main basse sur le Cameroun (1972), on the repression of the UPC and the rule of Ahidjo, was seized by the French government, and he could not go home. He returned to Cameroon in 1991, opened a bookshop in Yaounde and kept writing against Biya's regime until his death.
sum: A Cameroonian novelist and essayist whose satires of colonial rule and missionaries, such as The Poor Christ of Bomba (1956), made him a major voice of African literature in French.
